en.html:
Yes. Indeed.

It all began when that man came back to the village after being away for so many years, carrying the title of shogunate magistrate like a medal on his chest.

A magistrate, specially sent to a tiny village like ours? Strange, no? Also worrying. But he was born here, so I told myself, at least he is one of ours. At first that was all I thought.

Very soon, though, I was knocked flat. This Nagasaka walked in with his men and straight away called all the village officials together and announced that he would dig up the mountain.

Yes, the mountain. There is an old story that a valuable vein is sleeping inside it. Long ago, when Lord Tokugawa was still ruling the land, a hunter found a precious stone there.

The people of that time were overjoyed. They called prospectors and wanted to start taking it out immediately. But a clan of <ruby>Emishi<rt>Emishi</rt></ruby> living on the mountain stood in front of them and said, stop.

The stone the hunter found, the Emishi told them, was the wrathful essence of <ruby>Konjin<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>. To dig it out was to invite the curse with your own hands.

The villagers could not feel the weight of such a warning. They closed their ears and followed the prospectors into digging a tunnel. Our village had nothing then, and it has nothing now. Perhaps seeing a tree that grows money suddenly, they went a little mad.

...And then the curse came down.

A terrible sight, they say. Just when the vein was about to be reached, lightning burst out of the mountain without warning and ran all over the area like a storm. Everyone that light touched...

Turned to stone, some say. Turned to sand, say others. Or <ruby>rusted away<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>. So many versions are told. One thing is certain: many people died. The records of that time leave no doubt about it.

The villagers lost their heads. They called the Emishi chief and begged him to calm the curse. Very convenient request, I know. But what we have heard is that the Emishi said not one word and agreed.

They placed their clan's sacred treasure, handed down from before, inside the tunnel as a weight to hold down <ruby>Konjin's<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby> essence, and then filled the tunnel back. Perhaps because of that, the curse came only that once and never again.

Even then the villagers could not feel safe. So they built a shrine on the mountain, handed it over to the Emishi, and had them worship the cursing god. That still continues. The shrine has become old and shabby, and the Emishi are much fewer now...

That is what happened, in the old days.

And this taboo, Nagasaka says he will touch. Digging a new hole from zero costs money and time, you see. So he studied the records and planned to dig out the old tunnel again.

Naturally, everyone opposed. Not because everybody believes the curse, mind you. It is an ancient story, and what part is true, who knows. Even I think so.

But listen. Suppose they really find the vein. What is waiting for us then? Only a miner's cruel life, no? And will <ruby>that<rt>・・</rt></ruby> Rokuhara send even a small share of the profit back to the village? I cannot believe it.

And if the whole legend of the curse is true... you understand, madam. Whichever way it turns, Nagasaka's plan can only bring unhappiness to this village.

Our objection was answered with a blade. What drove him so hard I do not know, but many who spoke against him were killed, and the previous headman also... Yes, I am his younger brother. Before all this I was only a general-store man.

When force is used, what contest can there be? The shogunate soldiers he brought were not so many, but there were also some other suspicious types with them. Bodyguards, you could say. And those ones were terribly strong...

We had no choice. We obeyed Nagasaka and started digging the mountain. Hard, hard work, with hardly any rest. From overwork, and from the punishments of the fellows who called it instruction, how many more died...

Resist and die. Obey and die. The village was pushed to the wall. And the work, shameless, was going smoothly. As if the gods were blessing Nagasaka alone. I am sure I was not the only one soaking his pillow in anger.

And while we were suffering like this... Madam Inspector, you came.

ja.html:
――左様でございます。
　そもそもの始まりは、長らく村を離れていたあの男
が、幕府代官の肩書きを引っさげて帰ってきたときの
こと。

　こんな小村にわざわざ代官が派遣されてくるなんて
おかしな話でございますし、厄介にも思いましたが、
それでも村の出身者というのが救いかと、最初はその
程度に考えておりました。

　しかしすぐ度肝を抜かれる羽目になったのでござい
ます。
　あの男、長坂は手勢を連れて乗り込んで来るや否や
村の諸役を集め、お山を掘ると言い放ったのですから。

　はい。
　あの山には貴重な鉱脈が眠っているという言い伝え
がございまして――昔、まだ徳川さまが天下を治めて
おられた頃、猟師が山で貴石を発見したということが。

　当時の村の人々は喜んで、山師を呼び寄せ、早速に
掘り出そうとしたようでございます。
　しかし、山に住んでいた<ruby>蝦夷<rt>えみし</rt></ruby>の一族がその前に立ち
塞がり、制止しました。

　なんでも猟師が発見した石は、蝦夷の言うところに
よると、<ruby>こんじんさま<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>の怒りの気なのだとか。
　それを掘り返すなど、望んで祟りを招くに等しいと。

　そう言われてもピンと来なかったのでしょう、村人
達は耳を貸さず、山師に従って坑道を掘り始めました。
　今も昔も何もない村のこと、やにわに金のなる木を
見つけて躍起になっていたのかもしれません。

　……そうして、祟りが降り注いだのでございます。

　それはそれは恐ろしい有様だったそうで。
　もうすぐ鉱脈に行き当たろうかというある時、不意
に山から稲光が迸るや、嵐のように辺りを駆け巡り、
その光に触れた者は皆……

　石になったやら、砂になったやら、<ruby>錆びてしまった<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>
やら、色々と伝えられておりますが。
　確かなことは、多くの者が亡くなったという、これ
は当時の記録からも疑いようのない事実でございます。

　村の者どもは慌てふためき、蝦夷の長を招いて祟り
を鎮めてくれるよう懇願しました。
　虫の良い言い草というものですが、蝦夷は何も口に
せず頼みを聞いてくれたと伝え聞いております。

　一族伝来の神宝を坑道の中に安置して<ruby>こんじんさま<rt>・・・・・・</rt></ruby>
の気を止める重石とし、その上で坑道を埋め戻したの
だそうで。
　その甲斐あってか、祟りは一度きりで絶えました。

　それでも村人は安心できなかったのでしょう、更に
山へ社を建てて蝦夷に預け、祟り神を祀らせました。
　これは今もまだ続いております。社は古ぼけ、蝦夷
はだいぶん数を減らしてしまいましたが……。

　そんなことがあったのでございます。

　この禁忌に、長坂は手をつけると云うのですよ。
　一から穴を掘るのでは金も時間も掛かりますからな。
記録を調べて、昔の坑道を掘り返そうという計画で。

　もちろん、誰もが反対しました。
　それは何も皆が皆、祟りを信じ込んでいた為という
のではございません。何しろ昔の話ですし、何がどこ
まで真実かは怪しいと、私なども思っております。

　しかしでございます。仮に首尾良く鉱脈を発見した
としても、待っているのは、鉱夫としての過酷な生活
だけでございましょう？　<ruby>あの<rt>・・</rt></ruby>六波羅がまさか、
収益の一部でも村へ還元してくれるとは思えませんし。

　そしてもし、祟りの伝説が全て事実だったなら……。
　おわかりでございましょう。長坂の計画はどう転ん
でも、村を不幸にしかしないのでございます。

　皆の不賛同は、刃で報われました。
　何が彼をそこまで駆り立てたのかはわかりませんが、
異を唱えた者が何人も殺され、先代の村長も……ええ、
私はその弟です。それまではただの雑貨屋でしたよ。

　力ずくで来られては、勝負になりますものか。代官
が連れてきた幕府の兵はさほど多くなかったのですが、
ほかにも怪しげな連中が幾人かおりまして。用心棒と
でもいうのでしょうかな。それがまた、滅法強く……。

　止むを得ず私どもは長坂に従い、お山を掘り始めた
のでございます。ろくに休みもなしの、苛酷な作業で
ございました。過労や、指導と称する奴らの制裁で、
また何人が死んだことか……。

　刃向かえば死。従っても死。
　村は追い込まれておりましたが、忌々しくも作業の
方は順調でした。長坂一人を神様が嘉したかのようで、
悔しさに枕を濡らしたのは私だけではありますまい。

　そうして難儀していたところに……
　巡察官さま、貴方がやって来られたのでございます。

en.html:
The headman's house was a reasonable size, and the reception room they showed us into was wide enough for a sumo bout. I suspect this came less from the master's wealth than from the village having more land than it knows what to do with.

As one would expect of a reception room, no conspicuous dirt was in evidence. It also had no furniture of any taste. Everything was very plain. That even the house where the village heads have lived, generation after generation, was only this much said enough about the village's poverty.

The headman seemed ill at ease, perhaps embarrassed by the bareness of the room. Personally I preferred the lack of decoration. But saying so would not please a man who is bare by necessity and not by choice.

And in truth, if he was uneasy, the reason probably lay elsewhere. The unknown outsider, myself, was hardly innocent. Still, the headman's eyes had been on our other guest for some time.

ja.html:
村長の家はまずまずの大きさで、通された応接間も
相撲くらいはできそうな広さがあった。といっても、
それは主人の財権力ゆえというより単に土地が余って
いるからというのが理由ではないだろうか。

　応接間だけに見苦しい汚れが目立つなどということ
はないが、気の利いた調度があるわけでもなかった。
　ごく質素な装いである。代々の村長が住まいとした
家にしてこれということからも、村の貧しさは窺えた。

　部屋の味気なさを恥じてか、村長は気後れしている
ようにも見えた。俺の嗜好で言えばこの飾り気の無さ
はむしろ好ましい。がそう口にしても、趣味でやって
いるわけではない村長にすれば喜べないだろう。

　それに実際のところ、村長が本当に気後れしている
のだとするなら、理由はもっと他にありそうだった。
　得体の知れない外来人（俺）も潔白ではなかろうが。
村長の視線は先刻から、もう一人の来客の上にあった。

en.html: A woman in her prime. Calling her beautiful caused me no difficulty at all. Her long hair was especially glossy. The way she picked up the teacup and her easy smile showed good breeding. And behind her sat an old woman who could not have looked more like an attendant. A picture-perfect lady from above the clouds, raised behind closed doors. But the picture had one flawflaw that was hard to overlook. Flaw may be the wrong word. It did not damage her appearance in the least. The military uniform suited her. It suited her so well that it made me tilt my head. A modern uniform is not armor from the age of warring states, but it still carries a smell of hardness, unrest and ill omen. It was strange that none of this clashed with this woman. The balance was right. Nothing unusual about the uniform itself, after all.◆ ............A foolish question.
en.text:
A woman in her prime. Calling her beautiful caused me no difficulty at all. Her long hair was especially glossy. The way she picked up the teacup and her easy smile showed good breeding. And behind her sat an old woman who could not have looked more like an attendant.

A picture-perfect lady from above the clouds, raised behind closed doors. But the picture had one flawflaw that was hard to overlook.

Flaw may be the wrong word. It did not damage her appearance in the least. The military uniform suited her. It suited her so well that it made me tilt my head.

A modern uniform is not armor from the age of warring states, but it still carries a smell of hardness, unrest and ill omen. It was strange that none of this clashed with this woman. The balance was right.

Nothing unusual about the uniform itself, after all.◆

............A foolish question.

en.html:
It was she who suited the uniform. She had the unrest and the ill omen in her own right. Whatever her appearance, she was without doubt a soldier.

The headman had been present earlier. If he remembered the gunshot, he could not now be confused, thinking she was a noble lady in costume. His discomfort must therefore come from the organization her uniform declared.

The International Union for Harmonious Coexistence and Prosperity, Yamato Occupation Forces General Headquarters. GHQ. Until six years ago, the enemy the entire nation had fought. Now, a pack of foreigners sitting on our heads as occupiers.

They also recognized Rokuhara as the ruler of Yamato and watched the nation fall apart in silence. Search to the bottom of the Ogasawara Trench and you would not find a reason to like them.

On top of that, this woman looked Yamato by every measure. That the words traitor and collaborator rose in the mind was only natural.

ja.html:
彼女の方が軍服に合っているのだ。
　不穏と不吉の気配を自前で持っているのだ。
　外観がどう見えようと、彼女は間違いなく軍人なの
だから。

　あの場には村長もいた。銃声の響いた一幕を覚えて
いるのなら、今更貴婦人の仮装と誤解して戸惑うこと
もないだろう。であれば彼の困惑は実のところ、軍服
が示す所属に帰せられるに違いない。

　国際統和共栄連盟／大和進駐軍司令部。通称ＧＨＱ。
　六年前までは国を挙げての戦争相手であり、現在は
占領者として頭上に君臨する、異邦人の群団。

　そして、六波羅を大和の統治者として認め、国家の
荒廃を黙視している存在。
　好意を抱くべき理由は小笠原海溝の底まで探しても
ありそうにない。

　かてて加えて、この女性は大和人以外のどんな人種
にも見えなかった。
　自然の帰結として、売国者、裏切者、といった言語
が思い浮かぶのは避けられないところである。
